items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: Sonny Gray was there. ... So, man, we struck up. I made a double-fought introduction.

ctx.x: You can get them all. All the drummers. You know, I said, I take them two drummers. One of one race, one of the other race. And when I get through pouring oil on you, brother, you never want to see Norm Downs or Baby Dots anymore. Never seen drummers. I work with good men. I work with, I haven't worked with no hands. I work with good men. Sure. We was working on 51st in Michigan. We had just left the Northside. Plantation Club? I'll never forget that as long as I live. Duke Everton and the gang came there. Bonny…
He said, you got a record of the top of my heart. I was supposed to. I know, he's nearly as tall as I am. He said, all the men have music. Sonny Gray was there.

So, I said, Ben, what do you want to play? I said, Duke, what are you going to play? I can't play no numbers. He said, just play in the numbers. He said, I'll play some. He picked up a number. So, I told Dave, I said, oh, Dave, you don't want no music to hear? He said, no. He said, no. And here's Dave, that's here. I always put him on there. Here's Sonny Gray on. Here's this side. Look at that. Look at that. That's that drummer that the government. So, man, we struck up. I made a double-fought introduction. Loud.…
